newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia IPP gas demand to hit 860,700 bln cubic feet.
newsitem.headline: Asia IPP gas demand to hit 860,700 bln cubic feet.

text.p: Asia's independent power producers (IPP) liquefied natural gas demand could reach 860,700 billion cubic feet after 2000, up by nearly a quarter from 1995, a senior company official said on Thursday.
Ronald Ripple, Vice President of Oregon-based Economic Insight Inc, told an Asian Gas conference there were 24 projects totalling 12,928 megawatts under construction in Asia.
He said most would be completed between 2000 and 2003 and would need 860,700 billion cubic feet of gas a year, a 23.72 percent rise in LNG usage from 1995.
In India five IPP projects with a total capacity of 4,063 megawatts would cause LNG demand to rise by over 40 percent, he said.
In Thailand, seven projects totalling 3,148 megwatts in capacity would spark a 65 percent rise in LNG demand.
He said the 24 projects are in China, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Pakistan, the Philippines and Thailand.
